items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: he, Rolini and Brodsky, between the three of them as a rhythm section, were great... And we even put on a record with Rolini... that's where the goofus five came from.

ctx.x: Well, that's interesting. The first one in the big bands around there.

The big band field, he used the press roll. And he was steady as a rock. He's the one that gave us our fundamental beat. Of course, he, Rolini and Brodsky, between the three of them as a rhythm section, were great. And we, of course, were far from attempting to create pure jazz. We used kazoos and every other instrument in the way of a novelty. We even put on a record with Rolini, playing it as a flute, instead of the pseudo-saxophone it was supposed to be, a thing called the coenophone. And I said, the recorder…
Well, this isn't too different from what the New Orleans boys had already found out about using novelty instruments, washboards, and so forth. Yeah. That have a great visual appeal.
